title: Two author-disjoint cache scales improve word prediction but miss historical count variation
statement: After training on Chaucer and selecting parameters on Gower, the two-cache model yields 8.754 bits/token on Malory and 11.053 on Shakespeare, compared with 9.190 and 11.720 for the development-selected single cache. Each independent test has 84,300 tokens and at least ten complete blocks at every width. All ten observed Taylor exponents exceed both control medians and the maximum across 32 richer-model samples. The external gate fails and this trial stops before manuscript comparison.
check: To test whether distributional shifts explain the remaining error, predeclare a normalized model with a slow chapter or topic component and a finite lexical cache. Use independently selected long historical works, check the same widths and multiple genres, and distinguish lexical coverage from time scales. Preserve the author-disjoint gate and do not compare manuscript data before the external test succeeds.
protocol:
# K-038-open-2 external two-scale calibration

One historical English training author, one development author, and two independent test authors. Role assignment is fixed by source scope and evidence of author separation before any measurements. Normalize ASCII lowercase word tokens as in the earlier benchmark. Use up to the first 100,000 training tokens and first 40,000 development tokens after documented extraction. Test the first common length 84,300 words if all test works support it, otherwise 67,440 words, and report unsupported below that floor. At 84,300 the five fixed widths give 30, 20, 15, 12 and 10 complete blocks without tail truncation.

Preserve the alpha=4 shrinkage of the previous model for the learned bigram and both sequential caches. The normalized base is 90% training unigram and 10% normalized training character Markov with pseudocount 0.2. Prevent an initial empty word and force an end at 128 characters. Report input tokens outside explicit support instead of silently dropping them. The cache predicts from previous tokens before updating with the target; generation uses its own previous output. Reset at each independent text. No test word counts are used to train the candidate model.

On development log loss compare no cache, a single finite cache with windows 256/1024/4096 and weights .1/.3/.5, and the richer candidate with first window 256/1024, second window 8192/16384, and weight grids short 0/.12/.24, long 0/.15/.3/.45 with total at most .65. Choose minimum mean development bits/token separately within single and two-scale grids. Within an exact tie choose fewer active caches and then smallest window/weight tuple. Freeze fitted parameters before scoring the test authors. Report the no-cache and single-cache held-out predictive losses as well as the selected richer loss.

Use the registered Taylor statistic over widths 2810/4215/5620/7025/8430, with complete blocks and nonzero sample-variance types only, based on the source implementation. Simulate 32 independent histories of the selected richer model, 32 exact-frequency permutations of each test work, and 32 test-fitted empirical first-order Markov samples of each test work. The last is a descriptive null distinct from the fit-only local loss baseline. For each test author and width require the actual exponent to exceed both null medians and fall within the predeclared central 90% model prediction envelope. Also report whole simulated extrema, dependent joint rank diagnostics, type counts, lengths, and support. Require local held-out bits/token no larger than the no-cache baseline per author. No manuscript comparison is allowed after external failure. If all checks pass, a separate adequately supported manuscript sampling plan is still necessary.

Also generate the development-selected single-cache model on the same test lengths and with the same number of replicates, for a matched multiscale comparator. This comparator does not change the richer model's preregistered gate.

evidence.metric_validation:
# Taylor metric verification for K-038-open-2

The source is Keito Yoshida's immutable calibration module at commit 8920f2e506fce4c2c5a1245fb21a312f25655f1b. The downloaded file matches the SHA-256 published by prior PR #713, 554276d115500f2960831ab45910d9fc1c9625e1d06ac79ccb37b0ca16d58545.

- [Yoshida calibration source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seeton/Voynich-public/8920f2e506fce4c2c5a1245fb21a312f25655f1b/analysis/calibration/taylor_metric.py)
- [Prior finite-cache experiment](https://github.com/Ayan-Bandyopadhyay/voynich-swarm/pull/713)

For width W and N input tokens, use B=floor(N/W) complete nonoverlapping blocks. Discard the tail and define the vocabulary from the used prefix. For each type, sum counts s1 and squared counts s2 across the B blocks, including zero where the type is absent. Its sample variance is (B·s2−s1²)/(B·(B−1)). Integer moments distinguish exact zero variance before regression. Fit log10(sample SD) on log10(mean count) by unweighted OLS with intercept, using only nonzero-variance types. Report the residual RMSE, observed and fitted type counts, used and discarded token counts, and complete block count. Fewer than two complete blocks, fewer than two fitted types, and identical fitted mean counts each make the estimate undefined.

The independent NumPy implementation agreed with the pinned scalar code on 19 evaluated fixtures, including a 13-token exact hand-checkable stream and three topic-shifted Zipf streams with 67,459, 84,317 and 96,601 tokens. The latter used each fixed width 2,810, 4,215, 5,620, 7,025 and 8,430, plus one string-ID check per stream. All integer fields agreed exactly. The largest absolute difference across exponent, intercept and RMSE was 3.33×10⁻¹⁶. Six error fixtures tested short or degenerate data and malformed parameters. The complete fixture comparison took about 1.071 seconds for the scalar code and 0.042 seconds for the vector code on this run.

The tiny input a a b c a b b d b c c d excluded at width four gives exponent 0.13274589158141123. It retains 12 tokens in three blocks, drops one tail token, and fits all four observed types. The widths overlap in their underlying data and the exponent is descriptive; fit support and historical gate decisions are reported separately. No manuscript text was inspected.

The source anthology is one test-author unit.

analysis: Development loss is 10.863 bits/token for weights .12 and .45 at windows 256 and 16384, versus 11.721 for the best single cache, window 4096 and weight .5.

The richer model fails all ten comparisons even using complete simulated ranges instead of the predeclared central 90% envelopes. In the matched single-cache comparison, only one of the ten observations across both authors falls inside the full generated range.

Each set of five widths is estimated on the same text and is dependent. The simultaneous rank diagnostic is reported with conservative ties and 33 ranks; it is distinct from the predeclared envelope criterion and is not a claim of a multiplicity-corrected confirmatory rejection.

About 8.7% of Malory tokens and 12.4% of Shakespeare tokens are unseen in training. Spelling regularization, dates, genre and lexical overlap differ. This tested combination falls short of the external gate. The relative contributions of these factors remain unresolved.
Three-role author separation and large blocks are verified. No exact 50-word sequence was shared between any pair of the first 100,000 normalized words per source.

The Taylor implementation reproduces the source scalar output to 3.33e-16 on 19 checks. The two-scale prediction matches 27 independently computed sequential probabilities and deterministic generation replays.

from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from dataclasses import asdict
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
from random import Random
import sys

import numpy as np

from cache_model import Model, loss
from taylor_metric import WIDTHS, compute_widths

WORK = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
MANIFEST = WORK / "sources" / "manifest.json"
TEST_LENGTHS = (84300, 67440)
DRAWS = 32
NO_CACHE = (256, 8192, 0., 0.)
SINGLE = [NO_CACHE] + [(w, 8192, a, 0.) for w in (256, 1024, 4096) for a in (.1, .3, .5)]
DOUBLE = [(s, l, a, b) for s in (256, 1024) for l in (8192, 16384)
          for a in (0., .12, .24) for b in (0., .15, .3, .45) if a + b <= .65]
WINDOWS = set(k for setting in SINGLE + DOUBLE for k in setting[:2])
KINDS = ("two_scales", "one_scale", "frequency_shuffle", "test_empirical_bigram")


def manifest():
    data = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text())["works"]
    counts = {}
    sets = {"train": [], "dev": [], "test": []}
    authors = set()
    for row in data:
        path = MANIFEST.parent / row["file"]
        raw = path.read_bytes()
        assert hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() == row["sha256"], row["id"]
        words = raw.decode().split()
        assert all(word.isascii() and word.isalpha() and word.islower() for word in words), row["id"]
        assert row["author"] not in authors
        authors.add(row["author"])
        counts[row["id"]] = len(words)
        sets[row["role"]].append((row["id"], words))
    assert len(sets["train"]) == len(sets["dev"]) == 1 and len(sets["test"]) >= 2
    return sets, counts


def fit(model, development):
    predictions = [model.predictive_parts(tokens, WINDOWS) for _, tokens in development]

    def rank(setting):
        s, l, a, b = setting
        value = float(np.mean([loss(parts, setting) for parts in predictions]))
        active = int(a > 0) + int(b > 0)
        return value, active, s, l, a, b

    ranked_short = sorted(rank(setting) for setting in SINGLE)
    ranked_long = sorted(rank(setting) for setting in DOUBLE)
    pick = lambda ranking: tuple(ranking[0][2:])
    return pick(ranked_short), pick(ranked_long), {"single": ranked_short, "double": ranked_long}


def estimates(words):
    out = compute_widths(words)
    return [asdict(out[width]) for width in WIDTHS]


def worker_init(train, tests, short, long):
    global MODEL, TESTS, SHORT, LONG, TEST_ROWS
    MODEL = Model(train)
    TESTS = tests
    SHORT, LONG = short, long
    TEST_ROWS = {}
    for name, words in tests:
        rows = {}
        for a, b in zip(words, words[1:]):
            rows.setdefault(a, []).append(b)
        TEST_ROWS[name] = rows


def empirical_bigram(words, rows, rng):
    output = [rng.choice(words)]
    for _ in range(len(words) - 1):
        output.append(rng.choice(rows.get(output[-1], words)))
    return output


def simulate(job):
    index, kind, seed = job
    name, words = TESTS[index]
    rng = Random(seed)
    if kind in ("two_scales", "one_scale"):
        candidate = MODEL.generate(len(words), LONG if kind == "two_scales" else SHORT, rng)
    elif kind == "frequency_shuffle":
        candidate = words.copy()
        rng.shuffle(candidate)
    else:
        candidate = empirical_bigram(words, TEST_ROWS[name], rng)
    return name, kind, {"seed": seed, "unique_tokens": len(set(candidate)), "stats": estimates(candidate)}


def min_rank_diagnostic(actual, peers):
    values = np.asarray([actual] + peers)
    tail_ranks = np.empty(values.shape, dtype=int)
    for i in range(len(values)):
        tail_ranks[i] = np.minimum((values >= values[i]).sum(axis=0),
                                   (values <= values[i]).sum(axis=0))
    most_extreme = tail_ranks.min(axis=1)
    return float(np.mean(most_extreme <= most_extreme[0]))


def summarise(actual, draws):
    table = []
    for i, observed in enumerate(actual):
        record = {"width": WIDTHS[i], "observed": observed}
        obs = observed["exponent"]
        for kind in KINDS:
            exponents = np.array([rep["stats"][i]["exponent"] for rep in draws[kind]])
            assert np.all(np.isfinite(exponents)) and np.isfinite(obs)
            lo, hi = np.quantile(exponents, [.05, .95])
            record[kind] = {
                "minimum": float(exponents.min()), "maximum": float(exponents.max()),
                "median": float(np.median(exponents)), "predictive_90": [float(lo), float(hi)],
                "within_range": bool(exponents.min() <= obs <= exponents.max()),
                "within_90": bool(lo <= obs <= hi),
                "add_one_upper_tail": (1 + int(np.count_nonzero(exponents >= obs))) / (1 + len(exponents)),
            }
        record["above_both_control_medians"] = (
            obs > max(record[kind]["median"] for kind in KINDS[2:])
        )
        table.append(record)
    obs = [part["exponent"] for part in actual]
    jointly = {kind: min_rank_diagnostic(obs, [[part["exponent"] for part in row["stats"]]
                                              for row in draws[kind]]) for kind in KINDS}
    return table, jointly


def main():
    smoke = "--smoke" in sys.argv
    sets, counts = manifest()
    training = sets["train"][0][1][:100000]
    development = [(name, words[:40000]) for name, words in sets["dev"]]
    assert len(training) >= 50000 and len(development[0][1]) >= 30000
    n = next((candidate for candidate in TEST_LENGTHS
              if all(len(words) >= candidate for _, words in sets["test"])), None)
    if n is None:
        raise ValueError("No predeclared test length is supported by all test authors")
    tests = [(name, words[:n]) for name, words in sets["test"]]
    model = Model(training)
    single, double, tuning = fit(model, development)
    report = {"test_length": n, "word_counts": counts, "training_length": len(training),
              "development_length": len(development[0][1]), "short": single,
              "long": double, "dev_loss_trials": tuning, "tests": {}}
    print("fit", single, double, "test length", n, flush=True)
    n_draws = 2 if smoke else DRAWS
    pending = [(i, kind, 410001 + 10000 * i + 100 * k + draw)
               for i in range(len(tests)) for k, kind in enumerate(KINDS)
               for draw in range(n_draws)]
    all_draws = {name: {kind: [] for kind in KINDS} for name, _ in tests}
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=3, initializer=worker_init,
                             initargs=(training, tests, single, double)) as pool:
        for index, (name, kind, draw) in enumerate(pool.map(simulate, pending)):
            all_draws[name][kind].append(draw)
            if (index + 1) % n_draws == 0:
                print("complete", name, kind, len(all_draws[name][kind]), flush=True)
    for name, words in tests:
        parts = model.predictive_parts(words, WINDOWS)
        local = {"no_cache": loss(parts, NO_CACHE),
                 "one_scale": loss(parts, single), "two_scales": loss(parts, double)}
        actual = estimates(words)
        table, jointly = summarise(actual, all_draws[name])
        gate = local["two_scales"] <= local["no_cache"] and all(
            width["above_both_control_medians"] and width["two_scales"]["within_90"] for width in table
        )
        report["tests"][name] = {
            "n_unique": len(set(words)),
            "n_oov_tokens": sum(word not in model.counts for word in words),
            "local_bits_per_token": local,
            "widths": table,
            "joint_rank_p": jointly,
            "gate": gate,
            "draws": all_draws[name],
        }
    report["external_gate"] = all(test["gate"] for test in report["tests"].values())
    report["replicates"] = n_draws
    (WORK / ("smoke.json" if smoke else "results.json")).write_text(
        json.dumps(report, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
    )
    print("external gate", report["external_gate"], flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from collections import Counter
from itertools import product
from random import Random
import math

import numpy as np

from cache_model import ALPHA, Model, loss

train = "these old words were written with other words and these words recur".split()
sample = "when old words recur these unrelated words can recur".split()
model = Model(train)
for symbol, (_, _, probabilities) in model.rows.items():
    assert math.isclose(sum(probabilities.values()), 1)
    assert ("$" not in probabilities) == (symbol == "$")
assert all(model.base_probability(word) > 0 for word in sample)
pknown = sum(model.base_probability(word) for word in set(train))
assert .9 < pknown < 1

parts = model.predictive_parts(sample, (2, 5))
manual = []
checks = 0
for i, word in enumerate(sample):
    base = model.base_probability(word)
    transitions = [b for a, b in zip(train, train[1:]) if i and a == sample[i - 1]]
    bigram = (transitions.count(word) + ALPHA * base) / (len(transitions) + ALPHA)
    histories = [sample[max(0, i - width):i] for width in (2, 5)]
    short, long = ((Counter(history)[word] + ALPHA * base) / (len(history) + ALPHA)
                   for history in histories)
    for a, b in zip((bigram, short, long), (parts[0][i], parts[1][2][i], parts[1][5][i])):
        assert math.isclose(a, b, rel_tol=1e-13)
        checks += 1
    manual.append(.43 * bigram + .27 * short + .30 * long)
assert math.isclose(loss(parts, (2, 5, .27, .30)), float(-np.log2(manual).mean()), rel_tol=1e-13)

for weights in product((0., .15), repeat=2):
    setting = (2, 5, *weights)
    first = model.generate(2000, setting, Random(79))
    second = model.generate(2000, setting, Random(79))
    assert first == second and all(word and word.isalpha() for word in first)
print(f"{checks} manual sequential probabilities, exact loss, normalized rows and deterministic generation")

taylor_metric.py.text:
"""Fixed-width word Taylor exponent with exact integer count moments.

Equivalent on nondegenerate inputs to Yoshida's archived implementation at
seeton/Voynich-public commit 8920f2e506fce4c2c5a1245fb21a312f25655f1b.
This module accepts already tokenized input and never constructs a page sample.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from numbers import Integral

import numpy as np


WIDTHS = (2810, 4215, 5620, 7025, 8430)
DEFAULT_WIDTH = 5620


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaylorEstimate:
    exponent: float
    intercept: float
    rmse: float
    width: int
    n_tokens: int
    n_windows: int
    n_used_tokens: int
    n_dropped_tokens: int
    n_observed_types: int
    n_fitted_types: int


def _encode(tokens):
    if isinstance(tokens, (str, bytes)):
        raise TypeError("tokens must be a sequence of token objects, not text")
    if isinstance(tokens, np.ndarray):
        if tokens.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError("tokens array must be one-dimensional")
        if tokens.size == 0:
            return np.empty(0, dtype=np.int64), 0
        if np.issubdtype(tokens.dtype, np.integer):
            lower, upper = int(tokens.min()), int(tokens.max())
            if lower >= 0 and upper < tokens.size:
                return tokens.astype(np.int64, copy=False), upper + 1

    # First-occurrence IDs handle arbitrary hashable tokens and sparse integers.
    vocabulary = {}
    ids = np.fromiter(
        (vocabulary.setdefault(token, len(vocabulary)) for token in tokens),
        dtype=np.int64,
    )
    return ids, len(vocabulary)


def _estimate(ids, vocabulary_size, width):
    if isinstance(width, bool) or not isinstance(width, Integral):
        raise TypeError("width must be an integer")
    width = int(width)
    if width <= 0:
        raise ValueError("width must be positive")
    n_tokens = len(ids)
    blocks = n_tokens // width
    if blocks < 2:
        raise ValueError("Taylor sample SD requires at least two complete windows")
    used = blocks * width

    # Every block counts absent types as zero. Integer moments preserve the
    # exact zero-variance exclusion before the floating-point logarithms.
    if used > 3_037_000_499:
        raise OverflowError("Taylor count moments exceed int64 range")
    totals = np.zeros(vocabulary_size, dtype=np.int64)
    sums_of_squares = np.zeros_like(totals)
    for start in range(0, used, width):
        counts = np.bincount(ids[start:start + width], minlength=vocabulary_size)
        totals += counts
        sums_of_squares += counts * counts
    variance_numerators = blocks * sums_of_squares - totals**2

    fit = variance_numerators > 0
    fit_totals = totals[fit]
    fitted = len(fit_totals)
    if fitted < 2:
        raise ValueError("Taylor regression requires at least two nonconstant types")
    if fit_totals.min() == fit_totals.max():
        raise ValueError("Taylor regression requires distinct fitted mean counts")
    x = np.log10(fit_totals / blocks)
    y = 0.5 * np.log10(variance_numerators[fit] / (blocks * (blocks - 1)))
    centered_x = x - x.mean()
    centered_y = y - y.mean()
    exponent = float(np.sum(centered_x * centered_y) / np.sum(centered_x**2))
    intercept = float(y.mean() - exponent * x.mean())
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((y - (intercept + exponent * x))**2)))
    return TaylorEstimate(
        exponent, intercept, rmse, width, n_tokens, blocks, used,
        n_tokens - used, int(np.count_nonzero(totals)), fitted,
    )


def compute_taylor(tokens, width=DEFAULT_WIDTH):
    """Compute one exponent. Degenerate fits raise ValueError."""
    ids, vocabulary_size = _encode(tokens)
    return _estimate(ids, vocabulary_size, width)


def compute_widths(tokens, widths=WIDTHS):
    """Compute estimates keyed by integer width using a shared vocabulary."""
    ids, vocabulary_size = _encode(tokens)
    return {int(width): _estimate(ids, vocabulary_size, width) for width in widths}

"""Rebuild four author-disjoint historical English samples from archived Gutenberg bytes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import unicodedata

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
RAW = HERE / "raw"
WORKS = [
    ("chaucer", "train", "Geoffrey Chaucer", "The Canterbury Tales", "late 14th century", 2383,
     "https://gutenberg.pglaf.org/2/3/8/2383/2383-0.txt", "Verse and prose in Purves's edition"),
    ("gower", "dev", "John Gower", "Confessio Amantis", "late 14th century", 266,
     "https://gutenberg.pglaf.org/2/6/266/266-0.txt", "Middle English narrative verse; Macaulay edition"),
    ("malory-1", "test", "Thomas Malory", "Le Morte d'Arthur, volume I", "written c. 1470; first printed 1485", 1251,
     "https://gutenberg.pglaf.org/1/2/5/1251/1251-0.txt", "Arthurian prose in a later edited spelling"),
    ("shakespeare", "test", "William Shakespeare", "The Complete Works, plays", "late 16th to early 17th century", 100,
     "https://gutenberg.pglaf.org/1/0/100/100-0.txt", "Early Modern English play dialogue; composite edition")
]
EXCLUSIONS = {
    "chaucer": (
        "Retain only the main Canterbury text. Drop editorial notes from each Notes to heading "
        "to the next narrative heading, bracketed passages, numbered footnote markers, notes in "
        "the right-hand gloss column, and the abridged Meliboeus, Parson and closing Prayer sections. "
        "Purves partly regularized spelling and the distinction between literary and editorial "
        "text follows the source layout."
    ),
    "gower": (
        "Retain the prologue and eight books between opening line and end marker. Drop underscore-marked "
        "Latin verse/rubrics, Latin Incipit/Explicit headings, bracketed inserts and line numbers."
    ),
    "malory-1": (
        "Retain prose between the unindented BOOK I. occurrence and the electronic-edition footer. "
        "Drop the table of contents, editorial note, Caxton's preface and chapter/book headings."
    ),
    "shakespeare": (
        "Retain verse and prose dialogue from plays with a Dramatis Personae heading and a subsequent "
        "opening ACT I; drop preliminary poems, cast lists, tables of contents, act/scene headings, "
        "standalone uppercase speaker names, bracketed stage directions and indented Enter/Exit/Exeunt "
        "stage paragraphs. The source anthology is one test-author unit."
    )
}


def digest(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def historical_words(text):
    replacements = str.maketrans({"œ": "oe", "æ": "ae", "þ": "th", "ð": "th", "ȝ": "gh"})
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text.casefold().translate(replacements))
    text = "".join(char for char in text if not unicodedata.combining(char))
    return re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text)


def chaucer(text):
    body = text.split("\nTHE CANTERBURY TALES.\n", 1)[1]
    body = body.split("\nTHE END OF THE CANTERBURY TALES\n", 1)[0]
    body = re.sub(r"\[[^\[\]]*\]", "", body, flags=re.S)
    retained = []
    notes = False
    omitted = False
    for line in body.splitlines():
        left = re.split(r" {3,}|\t+", line.lstrip(), 1)[0]
        phrase = re.sub(r"<\d+>", "", left).strip()
        if re.match(r"^notes\s+to\b", phrase, flags=re.I):
            notes = True
        elif (phrase.isupper() and re.match(r"^(?:THE|CHAUCER’S|PROLOGUE|EPILOGUE)\s+", phrase)
              and len(phrase) <= 90):
            notes = False
            if ("MELIB" in phrase or "PARSON’S" in phrase or "PRAYER OF CHAUCER" in phrase):
                omitted = True
            elif any(key in phrase for key in ("TALE", "PROLOGUE", "EPILOGUE")) and phrase not in {
                "THE TALE.", "THE TALE", "THE PROLOGUE.", "THE PROLOGUE",
                "THE EPILOGUE.", "THE EPILOGUE",
            }:
                omitted = False
            continue
        elif not notes and not omitted:
            retained.append(phrase)
    return "\n".join(retained)


def gower(text):
    body = text.split("\nOf hem that writen ous tofore\n", 1)[1]
    body = "Of hem that writen ous tofore\n" + body.split("[End of CONFESSIO AMANTIS]", 1)[0]
    body = re.sub(r"_[^_]*_", "", body, flags=re.S)
    body = re.sub(r"\[[^\[\]]*\]", "", body, flags=re.S)
    return "\n".join(line for line in body.splitlines()
                     if not re.match(r"^\s*(?:Incipit|Explicit)\s", line))


def malory(text):
    body = text.split("\nBOOK I.\n", 1)[1]
    body = body.split("\nEnd of the Project Gutenberg EBook", 1)[0]
    blocks = re.split(r"\n\s*\n", body)
    return "\n".join(block for block in blocks if not re.match(r"\s*(?:CHAPTER|BOOK)\s+[IVXLCDM]+\.", block))


def shakespeare(text):
    first_body = re.search(r"^THE SONNETS\s*$", text, flags=re.M)
    assert first_body
    header = text[:first_body.start()]
    contents = header.split("\n                    Contents\n", 1)[1]
    titles = frozenset(line.strip() for line in contents.splitlines() if line.strip())
    lines = text[first_body.start():].splitlines()
    sections = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line and not line[0].isspace() and line.strip() in titles:
            sections.append((line.strip(), i))
    selected = []
    for (_, start), (_, stop) in zip(sections, sections[1:] + [("END", len(lines))]):
        part = "\n".join(lines[start+1:stop])
        cast_head = re.search(r"^\s*Dramatis Person(?:æ|ae)\s*$", part, re.M)
        if not cast_head:
            continue
        part = part[cast_head.end():]
        first_act = re.search(r"^ACT I\.?\s*$", part, re.M)
        if not first_act:
            continue
        part = part[first_act.end():]
        part = part.split("*** END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK", 1)[0]
        part = re.sub(r"\[[^\[\]]*\]", "", part, flags=re.S)
        part = re.sub(r"^ +(?:Enter|Re-enter|Exit|Exeunt|Flourish|Alarum|Sennet)\b[^\n]*(?:\n +[^\n]+)*",
                      "", part, flags=re.M)
        for line in part.splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if line and not line.isupper() and not re.match(r"^(?:ACT|SCENE)\s+[IVXLCDM]+\b", line):
                selected.append(line)
    return "\n".join(selected)


PARSERS = {"chaucer": chaucer, "gower": gower, "malory-1": malory, "shakespeare": shakespeare}


def main():
    rows = []
    for identifier, role, author, title, date, ebook, url, genre in WORKS:
        raw_name = f"{identifier}.txt"
        raw = (RAW / raw_name).read_bytes()
        decoded = raw.decode("utf-8-sig").replace("\r\n", "\n")
        assert "*** START OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK" in decoded
        assert "*** END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK" in decoded, (identifier, "incomplete archive")
        narrative = PARSERS[identifier](decoded)
        words = historical_words(narrative)
        maximum = max(map(len, words))
        assert maximum <= 30, (identifier, maximum)
        assert len(words) >= {"train": 50_000, "dev": 30_000, "test": 84_300}[role], (identifier, len(words))
        encoded = ("\n".join(words) + "\n").encode()
        file = f"{identifier}.txt"
        (HERE / file).write_bytes(encoded)
        rows.append({
            "id": identifier, "role": role, "author": author, "title": title,
            "date": date, "genre": genre, "url": url, "catalog_url": f"https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/{ebook}",
            "license": "Public domain in the United States per Project Gutenberg catalogue",
            "raw_file": f"raw/{raw_name}", "raw_sha256": digest(raw),
            "raw_bytes": len(raw), "file": file, "sha256": digest(encoded), "tokens": len(words),
            "selection": EXCLUSIONS[identifier],
            "maximum_word_characters": maximum,
        })
        print(identifier, role, len(words), maximum, digest(encoded))
    manifest = {
        "selection_frozen": "Disjoint authors and fixed roles chosen by availability, clean documentation and length before model fitting or metrics.",
        "normalization": "Case-fold, transliterate five historical Latin-script letters, remove combining marks, and take contiguous ASCII lowercase alphabetic runs.",
        "works": rows,
    }
    (HERE / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
